title: Feedback Zipline: priority log & synthesis
body:
Executive snapshot:

This is a compact, action-focused synthesis of customer feedback gathered between 2026-08-01 and 2026-09-10 across support tickets, CSM calls, product surveys, and an enterprise beta cohort. Goal: produce a small set of candidate fixes (quick wins + medium bets) that the eng/product triage can intake in the next planning cycle.

High-level signals (3 top themes):
1) Predictability gaps for Dedicated capacity under variable burst loads — customers see tail latency outliers when autoscale engages.
 - Source: 7 enterprise incidents, 12 SRE field notes, 2 direct CSM escalations.
 - Representative quote: "We relied on reserved throughput but during marketing spikes the tail latency spiked to 8s — we lost live chat quality."

2) Observability blind spots around per-request token-cost attribution and KV-cache hit/miss breakdowns — engineering teams cannot reconcile billing vs observed behavior.
 - Source: customer analytics requests, 16 support threads, product survey.
 - Representative quote: "Token bill is up but we can't see which routes or prefixes caused it; dashboard numbers don't map to our logs."

3) Prompt templating + structured output ergonomics for hosted API users — customers want first-class patterns for function/tool-calling + deterministic schema validation.
 - Source: feature-ask ballots, 9 product interviews.
 - Representative quote: "We want a small library and examples that guarantee structured JSON output so our downstream pipelines don't break."

Priority-annotated feature requests (shortlist):
A. Autoscale tail-mitigation flags (quick guardrails)
 - What: Add an optional "burst-protection" autopolicy that temporarily routes to compatible lower-cost model variants and/or throttles non-critical queues during autoscale transitions.
 - Why: Reduces tail latency spikes and prevents large infra churn during unpredictable bursts.
 - Evidence: 7 incidents; 3 customers asked for this specifically.
 - Estimated effort: small-medium (2 sprint dev + 1 sprint config + SRE validation).
 - Business impact: High for Dedicated customers on reserved plans (reduces breach risk of SLAs).
 - Suggested owner: eng-serving-runtime + product-dedicated.

B. Token attribution drilldown panel (observability)
 - What: Per-route token billing breakdown with selectable time windows, ability to map to request IDs and KV-cache hit rates; CSV export.
 - Why: Removes reconciliation friction and reduces billing disputes.
 - Evidence: 16 threads complaining about mismatch; 4 customers escalated to billing.
 - Estimated effort: medium (dashboard+api+export; ~3 sprints across front-end+backend+analytics).
 - Business impact: Medium-High (reduces CS time and churn risk).
 - Suggested owner: observability + product-hosted-api.

C. Structured-output templates + reference patterns (DX kit)
 - What: Packaged prompt templates, sample tool-calling flows, test harness for schema conformance and sample SDK helpers.
 - Why: Lowers integration time for hosted API customers and reduces downstream parsing errors.
 - Evidence: Recurrent ask in developer interviews and support.
 - Estimated effort: small (1 sprint writing + 1 sprint docs + examples).
 - Business impact: Medium (improves time-to-value for PLG adoption).
 - Suggested owner: developer-experience + product-hosted-api.

Quick wins (can ship in 2 weeks):
 - Add a small column in the Console request table for "KV-cache hit?" (front-end flag fed by an existing header) — low dev cost, immediate visibility.
 - Publish a short cookbook: "Structured outputs: 5 patterns we recommend" with code snippets for JS/Python.
 - Add a canned CS response template for customers disputing token bills, including steps to gather artifacts.

Medium bets (4–12 weeks):
 - Implement token attribution drilldown (B).
 - Prototype burst-protection autopolicy with a canary group and metric dashboard (A).
 - Add a server-side validation hook for hosted API that can be toggled per-route to enforce JSON schemas for outputs.

Risk flags / constraints:
 - Autoscale policy changes carry customer risk: need clear opt-in and observable fallbacks. Must coordinate with sales/legal for SLA language changes.
 - Token attribution requires careful alignment with billing systems; different customers use different time-zone/aggregation windows — edge cases to validate.
 - Templates/tooling must avoid being framed as "trusted parsing" for sensitive user data; include privacy guidance.

Signal provenance (compact):
 - Support tickets: 28 tickets (IDs redacted) flagged as "billing" or "latency" between Aug 1—Sep 10, 2026.
 - Beta cohort: 6 enterprise customers provided structured feedback in week-of-2026-08-18 syncs.
 - CS interviews: 9 conducted; notes stored in Confluence.
 - Quick survey: 112 responses (hosted-users), 18% cited observability as top friction.

Suggested next steps (for triage meeting):
 1) Rapidly approve 3 quick-win tasks and assign owners (CS to create tickets with minimal acceptance criteria).
 2) Kick a 2-week spike for autoscale burst-policy prototype (eng-serving-runtime + SRE).
 3) Prioritize token-attribution into roadmap backlog; scope as cross-functional epic (observability, billing, console).
 4) Schedule a joint customer readout with 3 affected customers to validate assumptions before wider rollout.

Proposed acceptance criteria (examples):
 - KV-cache column: visible in Console for last 7 days; clicking links to request details with header trace.
 - Burst-protection pilot: reduces 95th/99th percentile tail latency by >=25% in canary traffic for at least 72 hours.
 - Token-attribution: billing export that reconciles to invoice totals within 1% for a 30-day window for pilot customers.

Open questions for PM/Eng discussion:
 - Which customers should be in the autoscale pilot (sensitivity to SLA penalties)?
 - Can we leverage existing cost-analytics pipelines for the token-attribution panel or must we build a dedicated path?
 - What level of schema enforcement is acceptable for hosted API customers before we introduce breaking changes?

Low-touch comms plan (CS + marketing):
 - Internal: CS one-pager + triage ticket with suggested talking points + Slack channel #cs-zipline.
 - External: short beta announcement to pilot participants and a roadmap note in the monthly product update.

Appendix: sample customer excerpts (anonymized)
 - "We turned on reserved capacity and still hit weird latency — our users noticed during peak campaign; autoscale didn't help quickly enough." — large e-comm platform.
 - "Our billing jumped 30% month-over-month; we found high token counts on a background route we thought was cached." — analytics vendor.
 - "Examples in the docs don't show function calling patterns that are realistic for our payloads; parsing errors cascade to our data lake." — fintech startup.

Document history / meta:
 - Compiled by: Aisha Patel (CS Field Signals).
 - Reviewed with: Marco Ruiz (SRE lead), Evelyn Chen (PM, Observability) on 2026-09-28.
 - Next edit planned after triage meeting on 2026-10-05.

Notes to self: attach CSV of disputed invoices (anonymized) and heatmap of tail-latency events from 2026-08-10—2026-09-10.

---
This doc is purposefully concise to speed decision-making; happy to expand any item into a full PRD or spike brief on request.
